## Notebook Overview

**Inputs:**

- `../../../data/acs_step2_2016_tract.feather` — 2012–2016 ACS measures on `tr2010_id`.
- `../../../data/acs_step2_2024_block_group_aggregated.feather` — 2020–2024 block-group measures aggregated to `tr2010_id`.
- `../../../data/acs_step2_2024_tract.feather` — Census-reported 2020–2024 tract measures on native `tr2020_id`.
- `../../../data/xwalk_tr20_tr10.feather` — statewide geographic-consistency flags and explicit tract links, keyed by `tr2020_id`.
- Existing `../../../data/acs_full.feather`, if saving is enabled and the file is present — column/type reference read before saving.

**Outputs:**

- Notebook-only `acs_diagnostics`, geographic coverage, source/change comparisons,
  and inventory comparisons; no diagnostic data files are written.
- Optional `../../../data/acs_full.feather` — the existing ACS tract panel: 2016 and block-group-aggregated 2024 measures
  (2016 dollars inflation-adjusted to 2024) side by side on `tr2010_id`, with
  change measures (level `*POST` ratios and share/rate `*PPC` percentage-point
  differences) and their coefficients of variation. `write_panel <- FALSE` is
  the default; the diagnostic workflow does not require a canonical output write.

This notebook:

1. Set up environment
2. Import and prepare survey measures
3. Merge surveys and calculate change variables
4. Review geographic coverage
5. Compare 2024 sources and implied changes (diagnostic only)
6. Compare occupied renter units and rental inventory (diagnostic only)
7. Validate the panel and optionally save

This step only **merges** existing tract measures and derives change variables;
all three ACS inputs already use the 14 counties configured and validated in
`02_assemble.Rmd`, so no further sample restriction happens here. This notebook
inherits county coverage from the 2016 input and checks both 2024 inputs on their
native keys and the full panel. County definitions remain centralized in stage 2.
Paired Census-vs-block-group comparisons use only geographically consistent
links, including consistent pairs with different GEOIDs. This restricts paired
diagnostic eligibility, not panel membership. Canonical 2024 values continue to
come from block groups; hierarchical selection and availability fallback are deferred.

# 1. Set up environment

## 1.1 Load packages

```{r load-packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
rm(list = ls())

library(here)          # project-root-relative paths via here::here()
library(Hmisc)
library(dplyr)
library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(spatstat)
library(matrixStats)
library(survey)
library(srvyr)
```

## 1.2 Load helper functions

This stage's helpers — feather I/O, the survey `merge_df()`, variable
renaming/selection, inflation adjustment, and the change-variable functions —
live in `R/merge_helpers.R`. That file is self-contained for this notebook (its
`merge_df()` differs from the one used by `02_assemble.Rmd`).
Shared geographic, key, and schema diagnostics live in `R/geography_qa.R`.
Diagnostic joins, geographic coverage, and paired summaries live in
`R/merge_diagnostics.R`; they do not change the canonical helpers.

```{r load-helpers}
source(here::here("R", "merge_helpers.R"))
source(here::here("R", "geography_qa.R"))
source(here::here("R", "merge_diagnostics.R"))
```

## 1.3 Set data directory and optional output write

Leave `write_panel <- FALSE` to run through all diagnostics and validate the
in-memory canonical panel. Setting it to `TRUE` explicitly enables the existing
canonical save path, with schema comparison and announced replacement. Diagnostic
fields never enter that file.

```{r set-paths}
data_dir <- here::here("..", "..", "..", "data")
write_panel <- FALSE
prior_panel_path <- file.path(data_dir, "acs_full.feather")
prior_panel <- if (isTRUE(write_panel) && file.exists(prior_panel_path)) {
  arrow::read_feather(prior_panel_path)
} else NULL
```

# 2. Import and prepare survey measures

## 2.1 Load and prepare 2020–2024 block-group-aggregated measures

Load the 2024 block-group-aggregated measures, suffix canonical variables with `_24`, and
keep the analytic variable set plus a few extra quality/derived columns
(`pct_miss_rent`, `pct_tc_rent`, `pct_miss_hval`, `tc_flag_rent_24`, `interp_rent`).
`pct_tc_rent` is the top-coded portion of `pct_miss_rent` (see §2.3/§2.6 of
`02_assemble.Rmd`). The analytic set now also carries the renamed multifamily count
`mf5E`, the non-single-family-attached count `nsfaE`, and the rental / for-sale
vacancy rates `pctrvacE` / `pctsvacE` (added to `rename_vars()` so they get the
year suffix). Preserve `rentE`, `rhuE`, and `rhu_inventoryE` separately with
`_24_bg_agg` suffixes for diagnostics before the canonical selection drops inventory.

```{r prep-24-bg-agg}
# # Load 2005-2009 ACS data
# rent_09 <- load_data(data_dir, NULL, "acs_09_step2.feather")

# Load 2020-2024 ACS data
acs_24_bg_agg <- load_data(data_dir, NULL, "acs_step2_2024_block_group_aggregated.feather")
report_n(acs_24_bg_agg, "2024 block-group-aggregated measures loaded")
assert_merge_measures(acs_24_bg_agg, "tr2010_id", "2024 block-group panel input")
input_keys_24_bg_agg <- acs_24_bg_agg$tr2010_id
acs_24_bg_agg_diagnostic <- acs_24_bg_agg |>
  select(tr2010_id, rentE, rhuE, rhu_inventoryE) |>
  rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_24_bg_agg"), -tr2010_id)

# Rename variables
acs_24_bg_agg <- rename_vars(acs_24_bg_agg, "24")

# Select variables
# var_list <- c("pct_miss_rent", "pct_tc_rent")
# var_list <- c("pct_miss_rent", "pct_miss_hval", "tc_flag_rent_24", "interp_rent", "interp_rentCV", "interp_rentM")
var_list <- c("pct_miss_rent", "pct_tc_rent", "pct_miss_hval", "tc_flag_rent_24", "interp_rent")
acs_24_bg_agg <- select_vars(acs_24_bg_agg, "24", var_list)

# Apply inflation adjustment
# n/a
```

## 2.2 Load Census-reported 2020–2024 tract measures

This source retains native 2020 geography and the documented post-censoring
`rentE`, occupied-renter `rhuE`, and `rhu_inventoryE`. These measures are kept
under explicit `_24_tract` names for diagnostics. Census tract `rentE` is a
direct median; the block-group counterpart is a weighted mean of block-group
medians. Use the upstream estimates without changing censoring or substituting
the separate interpolated-rent measure.

```{r prep-24-tract}
acs_24_tract <- load_data(data_dir, NULL, "acs_step2_2024_tract.feather")
report_n(acs_24_tract, "2024 Census tract measures loaded")
assert_merge_measures(acs_24_tract, "tr2020_id", "2024 Census tract input")
input_keys_24_tract <- acs_24_tract$tr2020_id
acs_24_tract_diagnostic <- acs_24_tract |>
  select(tr2020_id, rentE, rhuE, rhu_inventoryE) |>
  rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_24_tract"), -tr2020_id)
assert_tract_keys(acs_24_tract_diagnostic, input_keys_24_tract,
                  "Prepared Census tract diagnostics", key = "tr2020_id")
```

## 2.3 Load and prepare 2012–2016 measures

### Decision: Inflation-adjust 2016 dollars to 2024 dollars

Dollar-denominated 2016 measures (median rent, lower-quartile contract rent,
median household income, median house value — estimates and their margins of
error) are multiplied by **1.307** to express them in 2024 dollars, so that
change variables in §3.2 compare *real* values across the two periods. The
adjustment is applied only to the 2016 vintage (`infl_adj_vars(..., "16")`).

Inflation adjustment uses CPI-U annual averages (BLS, CPI-U, U.S. city average,
all items) to adjust 2016 dollars to 2024 dollars. Factor = 313.689 / 240.007 ≈
1.307.

```{r prep-16}
# Load 2012-2016 ACS data
acs_16 <- load_data(data_dir, NULL, "acs_step2_2016_tract.feather")
report_n(acs_16, "2016 tract measures loaded")
assert_merge_measures(acs_16, "tr2010_id", "2016 panel input")
input_keys_16 <- acs_16$tr2010_id
acs_16_diagnostic <- acs_16 |>
  select(tr2010_id, rentE, rhuE, rhu_inventoryE) |>
  rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_16"), -tr2010_id)
panel_counties <- sort(unique(substr(input_keys_16, 3, 5)))
stopifnot("Run stage 2 with all 14 configured counties before merging" = length(panel_counties) == 14L)
report_tract_counties(acs_16, panel_counties, "2016 input counties (validated in stage 2)")
report_tract_counties(acs_24_bg_agg, panel_counties, "2024 block-group destination counties")
report_tract_counties(acs_24_tract, panel_counties, "2024 Census tract counties", key = "tr2020_id")

# Rename variables
acs_16 <- rename_vars(acs_16, "16")

# Select variables
var_list <- c("m_flag_rent" , "m_flag_lqcrent", "m_flag_rhu", "m_flag_med_hval",
               "zero_flag_rhu", "tc_flag_rent", "tc_flag_lqcrent", "tc_flag_med_hval")
acs_16 <- select_vars(acs_16, "16", var_list)

# Apply inflation adjustmen
summary(acs_16$rentE_16)
acs_16 <- infl_adj_vars(acs_16, "16")
summary(acs_16$rentE_16)
stopifnot(identical(acs_16_diagnostic$tr2010_id, acs_16$tr2010_id))
acs_16_diagnostic$rentE_16 <- acs_16$rentE_16

# table(acs_16$m_flag1_16, useNA="ifany")
```

# 3. Merge surveys and calculate change variables

## 3.1 Merge 2016 and block-group-aggregated 2024 measures

### Decision: Keep all tracts (full join, not inner join)

The two surveys are full-joined on `tr2010_id` and **all** tracts are retained —
the inner-join filter (`filter(merge=="both")`) is intentionally left commented
out. Tracts present in only one period keep `NA` for the other period's measures;
change variables (§3.2) are guarded so they are `NA` when a base value is
missing or zero. There is therefore **no row-dropping filter** in this notebook.

Membership is audited against `input_keys_16` and `input_keys_24_bg_agg`, captured on
import. The expected panel key set is their union, with one row per tract.
`panel_membership` reports every one-period-only tract and county-level counts.
The output's existing constant-`TRUE` `base_id` is preserved as part of its
schema; it is not used to infer presence in the earlier survey.

```{r merge-surveys}
# Merge post rent data
n_16 <- nrow(acs_16)
n_24_bg_agg <- nrow(acs_24_bg_agg)
assert_tract_keys(acs_16, input_keys_16, "Prepared 2016 input")
assert_tract_keys(acs_24_bg_agg, input_keys_24_bg_agg, "Prepared 2024 block-group input")
acs_16_24_bg_agg <- merge_df(acs_16, acs_24_bg_agg)
table(acs_16_24_bg_agg$merge)
panel_membership <- audit_panel_keys(acs_16_24_bg_agg, input_keys_16, input_keys_24_bg_agg)
cat(sprintf("Merged %s (2016) and %s (2024 block-group) tracts -> %s panel rows\n",
            formatC(n_16, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
            formatC(n_24_bg_agg, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
            formatC(nrow(acs_16_24_bg_agg), format = "d", big.mark = ",")))

# Keep all
acs_16_24_bg_agg <- acs_16_24_bg_agg |>
  # dplyr::filter(merge=="both") |>
  select(-c(merge)) |>
  mutate(base_id=TRUE)

acs_full <- acs_16_24_bg_agg

# rent_full <- full_join(rent_16_24, rent_09,
#                   by = "tr2010_id") %>%
#   mutate(
#     merge = case_when(
#       base_id & pre_id ~ "both",
#       base_id ~ "base",
#       pre_id ~ "pre"
#     ),
#     .keep = "unused"
#   ) %>%
#   as_tibble()
# table(rent_full$merge)
# # all but 20 of the base tracts merged the post- tracts merged
# # 97% of tracts w/ rent data in 2016 have rent data for pre and post

# # Keep all
# acs_full <- acs_full |>
#   # dplyr::filter(merge=="both") |>
#   select(-c(merge))
```

## 3.2 Calculate change variables and their CVs

### Decision: Level changes are ratios; share / rate changes are percentage-point differences

Dollar- and count-denominated change ("POST") variables are the ratio of the
2024 value to the (inflation-adjusted) 2016 value, defined only where the 2016
denominator is positive (otherwise `NA`).

Share and rate change variables are instead **percentage-point differences**
(`value_24 - value_16`, named `*PPC`): the renter-occupied share `pctrhuPPC`, the
overall vacant share `pctvacPPC`, and the rental / for-sale vacancy rates
`pctrvacPPC` / `pctsvacPPC`. A difference is the natural change for a rate, is
defined wherever both periods are present (so it avoids the large zero-base `NA`
counts a ratio produces for rates that are often `0`), and is bounded in roughly
[−1, 1]. The carried `mf5E` / `nsfaE` counts are levels only and get no change
variable.

`m_flag_rentPOST` / `m_flag_rhuPOST` mark missing change values. Coefficients of
variation for the key (level) change variables come from ratio-MOE propagation in
`calc_cv_change_vars()`; the share / rate `*PPC` differences carry no CV.

```{r change-vars}
# Calculate change variables
acs_full <- calc_change_vars(acs_full)

table(acs_full$m_flag_rentPOST)
table(acs_full$m_flag_rhuPOST)

# Quick distribution check on the share / rate percentage-point changes
# (expected range roughly [-1, 1])
summary(acs_full$pctrhuPPC)
summary(acs_full$pctvacPPC)
summary(acs_full$pctrvacPPC)
summary(acs_full$pctsvacPPC)

# Calculate CV for change variables
acs_full <- calc_cv_change_vars (acs_full)
```

```{r summarize-cv}
print("Summary Stats: CV, 2016 Rental housing units ")

summary(acs_full$rhuCV_24)

summary(acs_full$rentCV_16)
print("Summary Stats: CV, 2024 Median rent ")
summary(acs_full$rentCV_24)

print("Summary Stats: CV, Rent change")
summary(acs_full$rentPOSTCV)
print("Summary Stats: CV, Rental housing unit change")
summary(acs_full$rhuPOSTCV)

print("Summary Stats: CV, Rent change")
summary(acs_full$interp_rentPOSTCV)
print("Summary Stats: CV, Rental housing unit change")
summary(acs_full$rhuPOSTCV)


print("Summary Stats: CV, 2016 Median household income ")
summary(acs_full$med_hhincCV_16)
print("Summary Stats: CV, 2024 Median household income ")
summary(acs_full$med_hhincCV_24)
```

# 4. Review geographic coverage

## 4.1 Load and validate geographic-consistency links

### Decision: Pair measurements only across exactly consistent geography

The analyst selected consistent pairs for source/change comparisons. The
crosswalk's non-missing double `geo_consistent` uses 0/1; `relationship_class`
uses `consistent`, `one_to_one_changed`, `split`, `merge`, and `many_to_many`.
Use those upstream classifications without redefining consistency. The explicit
2010 link, rather than equal GEOID text, aligns a consistent pair.

A split repeats a 2010 key. Collapse only agreeing status/class records before
attaching status to the panel; do not choose a split's Census measurement.
Merge/many-to-many records omit their 2010 partners, so this product cannot fully
classify the 2010 panel. Unresolved panel status remains `NA`, not zero or an
inferred class. Counts for all five classes are available on native 2020 tracts.

```{r load-geography}
tract_geography <- load_data(data_dir, NULL, "xwalk_tr20_tr10.feather")
report_n(tract_geography, "Statewide 2020-tract geographic-consistency input")
geography_links <- prepare_merge_geography(tract_geography)
print(table(tract_geography$geo_consistent, useNA = "ifany"))
print(table(tract_geography$relationship_class, useNA = "ifany"))
```

## 4.2 Attach statuses and source-specific diagnostic measures

`acs_diagnostics` is the full canonical panel plus notebook-only status and
source-specific columns. Every join below must preserve its 2010 keys and rows.
Only consistent links supply `tr2020_id` and Census measures. A missing Census
value may therefore reflect no eligible link, an absent source record, or a
missing estimate in an existing record; coverage tables distinguish these cases.

```{r build-diagnostic-panel}
acs_diagnostics <- merge_diagnostic_left_join(
  acs_full, geography_links$statuses, "tr2010_id", "Attach available panel statuses"
)
acs_diagnostics <- merge_diagnostic_left_join(
  acs_diagnostics, geography_links$consistent, "tr2010_id", "Attach consistent Census links"
)
acs_diagnostics <- merge_diagnostic_left_join(
  acs_diagnostics, select(acs_16_diagnostic, tr2010_id, rhu_inventoryE_16),
  "tr2010_id", "Attach 2016 diagnostic inventory"
)
acs_diagnostics <- merge_diagnostic_left_join(
  acs_diagnostics, acs_24_bg_agg_diagnostic, "tr2010_id", "Attach block-group diagnostic measures"
)
acs_diagnostics <- merge_diagnostic_left_join(
  acs_diagnostics, acs_24_tract_diagnostic, "tr2020_id", "Attach consistent Census measures"
) |>
  mutate(
    in_16 = tr2010_id %in% input_keys_16,
    in_24_bg_agg = tr2010_id %in% input_keys_24_bg_agg,
    in_24_tract = tr2020_id %in% input_keys_24_tract,
    geo_status = case_when(geo_consistent == 1 ~ "consistent",
                           geo_consistent == 0 ~ "not_consistent", .default = NA_character_)
  )
assert_tract_keys(acs_diagnostics, union(input_keys_16, input_keys_24_bg_agg),
                  "Full diagnostic panel")
stopifnot("Canonical columns must remain identical" =
            identical(select(acs_diagnostics, all_of(names(acs_full))), acs_full))

acs_24_tract_geography <- merge_diagnostic_left_join(
  acs_24_tract_diagnostic,
  select(tract_geography, tr2020_id, geo_consistent, relationship_class),
  "tr2020_id", "Native Census tract coverage", left_key = "tr2020_id"
)
```

## 4.3 Report native and panel coverage separately

Each class/status share uses all rows in its labeled universe. Panel class
counts for merge/many-to-many cannot be recovered from the omitted 2010 IDs;
their displayed zeros do not establish absence. `status_missing` records remain
in the denominator. Target crosswalk summaries use 2020 county membership and
do not alter statewide links or panel membership.

```{r geography-coverage}
target_tract_geography <- tract_geography |>
  filter(substr(tr2020_id, 3, 5) %in% panel_counties)
report_n(target_tract_geography, "Target-county native 2020 crosswalk (coverage only)")
geography_coverage <- list(
  statewide_crosswalk = summarize_merge_geography(tract_geography, "Statewide 2020 crosswalk"),
  target_crosswalk = summarize_merge_geography(target_tract_geography, "Target-county 2020 crosswalk"),
  census_input = summarize_merge_geography(acs_24_tract_geography, "2024 Census input, native 2020 keys"),
  full_panel = summarize_merge_geography(acs_diagnostics, "Full 2010 panel, partially resolved statuses")
)
walk(geography_coverage, function(result) {
  print(result$classes, n = Inf, width = Inf)
  print(result$status, n = Inf, width = Inf)
})

geography_unmatched <- list(
  panel_without_status = anti_join(select(acs_full, tr2010_id), geography_links$statuses, by = "tr2010_id"),
  statuses_outside_panel = anti_join(geography_links$statuses, acs_full, by = "tr2010_id"),
  census_without_crosswalk = anti_join(acs_24_tract_diagnostic, tract_geography, by = "tr2020_id"),
  target_crosswalk_without_census = anti_join(target_tract_geography, acs_24_tract_diagnostic, by = "tr2020_id"),
  consistent_panel_without_census = acs_diagnostics |>
    filter(geo_consistent == 1, !in_24_tract) |> select(tr2010_id, tr2020_id),
  consistent_census_outside_panel = geography_links$consistent |>
    semi_join(acs_24_tract_diagnostic, by = "tr2020_id") |>
    anti_join(acs_full, by = "tr2010_id")
)
iwalk(geography_unmatched, function(rows, label) {
  report_n(rows, paste("Unmatched:", label))
  print(head(rows, 20), width = Inf)
})
cat("Complete unmatched-key tables are retained in geography_unmatched; up to 20 rows shown above.\n")

alignment_coverage <- imap_dfr(
  diagnostic_groups(acs_diagnostics, "geo_status", c("consistent", "not_consistent")),
  function(mask, group) {
    x <- acs_diagnostics[mask, ]
    tibble(group = group, n_total = nrow(x),
           n_no_consistent_link = sum(is.na(x$tr2020_id)),
           n_consistent_link_without_census = sum(!is.na(x$tr2020_id) & !x$in_24_tract),
           n_census_record = sum(x$in_24_tract),
           n_census_rent_missing_in_record = sum(x$in_24_tract & is.na(x$rentE_24_tract)),
           n_census_inventory_missing_in_record = sum(x$in_24_tract & is.na(x$rhu_inventoryE_24_tract)),
           n_bg_record_absent = sum(!x$in_24_bg_agg))
  }
)
stopifnot(with(alignment_coverage,
               all(n_no_consistent_link + n_consistent_link_without_census + n_census_record == n_total)))
print(alignment_coverage, n = Inf, width = Inf)

native_tract_measure_coverage <- summarize_diagnostic_measures(
  acs_24_tract_geography, c("rentE_24_tract", "rhu_inventoryE_24_tract"),
  "relationship_class", merge_relationship_classes
)
print(native_tract_measure_coverage, n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

# 5. Compare 2024 sources and implied changes (diagnostic only)

## 5.1 Compare median rent and rental inventory levels

The full panel is the denominator for overall and geographic-status coverage.
Source summaries use each source's available values; paired differences and
correlations use both observed values on consistent links. Census values on
unpaired changed geography remain available in the native-source coverage table
in §4.3. A zero paired count outside consistent geography means the comparison
is unavailable, not that the native Census measure is missing.

For every comparison, `x` is the first measure and `y` the second:
`difference = x - y`, `absolute_difference = abs(x - y)`, and `ratio = x / y`
only where `y > 0`. Here x is Census tract and y is block-group aggregated.
The ratio equals 1 at agreement. The returned `values` tables retain tract keys;
`coverage` and `summaries` report counts and distributions without complete-case
filtering. Correlation is Pearson on paired observations and is `NA` for fewer
than two pairs or a constant measure. Empty/all-missing summaries are `NA`.

```{r compare-source-levels}
source_level_diagnostics <- list(
  rent = compare_diagnostic_measures(acs_diagnostics, "rentE_24_tract", "rentE_24_bg_agg",
                                     "geo_status", c("consistent", "not_consistent")),
  inventory = compare_diagnostic_measures(acs_diagnostics, "rhu_inventoryE_24_tract", "rhu_inventoryE_24_bg_agg",
                                          "geo_status", c("consistent", "not_consistent"))
)
walk(source_level_diagnostics, function(result) {
  print(result$coverage, n = Inf, width = Inf)
  print(result$summaries, n = Inf, width = Inf)
})
```

## 5.2 Compare implied 2016-to-2024 change ratios

### Decision: Preserve the established level-change definition in diagnostics

Diagnostic rent, inventory, and occupied-renter changes are 2024/2016 ratios,
defined only for positive observed baselines. Rent uses the same already-adjusted
2016 dollars as canonical `rentPOST`; counts receive no inflation adjustment.
Each concept uses its own 2016 baseline. No diagnostic ratio replaces a canonical
change variable, and no inventory MOE/CV is constructed.

```{r diagnostic-change-vars}
acs_diagnostics <- acs_diagnostics |>
  mutate(
    diag_rentPOST_24_tract = diagnostic_ratio(rentE_24_tract, rentE_16),
    diag_rentPOST_24_bg_agg = diagnostic_ratio(rentE_24_bg_agg, rentE_16),
    diag_rhu_inventoryPOST_24_tract = diagnostic_ratio(rhu_inventoryE_24_tract, rhu_inventoryE_16),
    diag_rhu_inventoryPOST_24_bg_agg = diagnostic_ratio(rhu_inventoryE_24_bg_agg, rhu_inventoryE_16),
    diag_rhuPOST_24_tract = diagnostic_ratio(rhuE_24_tract, rhuE_16),
    diag_rhuPOST_24_bg_agg = diagnostic_ratio(rhuE_24_bg_agg, rhuE_16)
  )
baseline_coverage <- imap_dfr(
  diagnostic_groups(acs_diagnostics, "geo_status", c("consistent", "not_consistent")),
  function(mask, group) {
    map_dfr(c("rentE_16", "rhu_inventoryE_16", "rhuE_16"), function(measure) {
      x <- acs_diagnostics[[measure]][mask]
      tibble(group = group, measure = measure, n_total = length(x),
             n_base_missing = sum(is.na(x)), n_base_nonpositive = sum(x <= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
             n_base_positive = sum(x > 0, na.rm = TRUE))
    })
  }
)
stopifnot(with(baseline_coverage, all(n_base_missing + n_base_nonpositive + n_base_positive == n_total)))
print(baseline_coverage, n = Inf, width = Inf)
source_change_diagnostics <- list(
  rent = compare_diagnostic_measures(acs_diagnostics, "diag_rentPOST_24_tract", "diag_rentPOST_24_bg_agg",
                                     "geo_status", c("consistent", "not_consistent")),
  inventory = compare_diagnostic_measures(acs_diagnostics, "diag_rhu_inventoryPOST_24_tract", "diag_rhu_inventoryPOST_24_bg_agg",
                                          "geo_status", c("consistent", "not_consistent"))
)
walk(source_change_diagnostics, function(result) {
  print(result$coverage, n = Inf, width = Inf)
  print(result$summaries, n = Inf, width = Inf)
})
```

# 6. Compare occupied renter units and rental inventory (diagnostic only)

## 6.1 Compare concepts within each native source and vintage

`rhuE` is renter-occupied units (B25003_003). `rhu_inventoryE` also includes vacant
for rent (B25004_002) and rented, not occupied (B25004_003). The tract products add
these estimates directly; block-group inventory allocates each with `wt_renthu`
and propagates any missing positive-weight contribution. Do not reconstruct
inventory from the block-group output's housing-weighted vacancy fields.

Each table uses its entire native input as denominator, including all 2024 Census
tracts regardless of geographic consistency. Here x is inventory and y is
occupied renter units. `n_x_below_y` and `share_x_below_y` report inventory below
occupied units; the share denominator is `n_paired`. Such observations are flagged
for review without changing either measure. Ratio exclusions include occupied
counts of zero; zero-baseline observations still enter differences and paired counts.

```{r compare-inventory-levels}
inventory_level_diagnostics <- list(
  tract_2016 = compare_diagnostic_measures(acs_16_diagnostic, "rhu_inventoryE_16", "rhuE_16"),
  bg_agg_2024 = compare_diagnostic_measures(acs_24_bg_agg_diagnostic, "rhu_inventoryE_24_bg_agg", "rhuE_24_bg_agg"),
  tract_2024 = compare_diagnostic_measures(acs_24_tract_diagnostic, "rhu_inventoryE_24_tract", "rhuE_24_tract")
)
iwalk(inventory_level_diagnostics, function(result, label) {
  cat("Native input:", label, "\n")
  print(result$coverage, n = Inf, width = Inf)
  print(result$summaries, n = Inf, width = Inf)
  if (any(result$coverage$n_x_below_y > 0)) {
    cat("REVIEW: inventory below occupied renter units; inspect this result's values table.\n")
  }
})
```

## 6.2 Compare inventory change with occupied-renter change

Compare the two concepts' change ratios using the full panel for block-group
2024 measures and separately the consistent subset for Census 2024 measures.
The full-panel source-change coverage in §5.2 retains information about all
excluded/unavailable Census comparisons. Here x is inventory change and y is
occupied-renter change; differences are differences between ratios, not changes
in unit counts or percentage-point changes. The canonical `rhuPOST` continues
to measure occupied-renter change.

```{r compare-inventory-changes}
consistent_diagnostics <- acs_diagnostics |> filter(geo_consistent == 1)
report_n(consistent_diagnostics, "Consistent subset for Census concept-change diagnostics only")
inventory_change_diagnostics <- list(
  bg_agg_full_panel = compare_diagnostic_measures(
    acs_diagnostics, "diag_rhu_inventoryPOST_24_bg_agg", "diag_rhuPOST_24_bg_agg"),
  tract_consistent = compare_diagnostic_measures(
    consistent_diagnostics, "diag_rhu_inventoryPOST_24_tract", "diag_rhuPOST_24_tract")
)
walk(inventory_change_diagnostics, function(result) {
  print(result$coverage, n = Inf, width = Inf)
  print(result$summaries, n = Inf, width = Inf)
})
```

# 7. Validate the panel and optionally save

Validate the in-memory panel and diagnostic invariants before the optional save.
The default run does not read an old saved panel as if it were the current result.

```{r validation-panel}
acs_out <- acs_full
assert_tract_keys(acs_diagnostics, acs_full$tr2010_id, "Diagnostic panel retains all canonical keys")
stopifnot("Diagnostic work must preserve every canonical column and value" =
            identical(select(acs_diagnostics, all_of(names(acs_full))), acs_full),
          "Block-group diagnostic rent change must agree with canonical rentPOST" =
            isTRUE(all.equal(acs_diagnostics$diag_rentPOST_24_bg_agg, acs_full$rentPOST)),
          "Block-group diagnostic occupied change must agree with canonical rhuPOST" =
            isTRUE(all.equal(acs_diagnostics$diag_rhuPOST_24_bg_agg, acs_full$rhuPOST)))
```

## 7.1 Check key uniqueness and duplicates

Expected: the panel is unique on `tr2010_id`.

```{r validate-keys-panel}
cat("acs_full:", nrow(acs_out), "rows |",
    n_distinct(acs_out$tr2010_id), "unique tr2010_id |",
    sum(duplicated(acs_out$tr2010_id)), "duplicate ids\n")
validated_panel_membership <- audit_panel_keys(acs_out, input_keys_16, input_keys_24_bg_agg)
report_tract_counties(acs_out, panel_counties, "In-memory panel destination counties")
```

## 7.2 Check missingness on critical variables

Expected: no missing `tr2010_id`. Missingness in the change ratios reflects
tracts present in only one period or with a non-positive base value; we report
counts rather than impose a threshold.

```{r validate-missingness-panel}
cat("acs_full missing tr2010_id:    ", sum(is.na(acs_out$tr2010_id)), "\n")
cat("acs_full missing rentE_16:     ", sum(is.na(acs_out$rentE_16)), "\n")
cat("acs_full missing rentE_24:     ", sum(is.na(acs_out$rentE_24)), "\n")
cat("acs_full missing rentPOST:     ", sum(is.na(acs_out$rentPOST)), "\n")
cat("acs_full missing interp_rentPOST:", sum(is.na(acs_out$interp_rentPOST)), "\n")
print(summarize_diagnostic_measures(
  acs_diagnostics, c("rentE_24_tract", "rentE_24_bg_agg", "rhu_inventoryE_16",
                     "rhu_inventoryE_24_tract", "rhu_inventoryE_24_bg_agg")
), n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

## 7.3 Check flag-variable encoding

The data-quality / change flags (`m_flag_*`, `zero_flag_*`, `tc_flag_*`) should
be numeric 0/1 (existing double storage), not string labels. The `base_id` / `post_id` columns are
join indicators (logical) and are reported for transparency. `base_id` is
constant `TRUE`; the input-key audit in §7.1 determines survey membership.

```{r validate-flags-panel}
flag_cols <- grep("^(m_flag_|zero_flag_|tc_flag_)", names(acs_out), value = TRUE)
for (f in flag_cols) {
  cat("acs_full", f, "-> class:", class(acs_out[[f]]),
      "| values:", paste(sort(unique(acs_out[[f]])), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
cat("acs_full base_id class:", class(acs_out$base_id),
    "| post_id class:", class(acs_out$post_id), "\n")
```

## 7.4 Summarize numeric variable distributions

Mean, min, and max for every numeric column in the panel. Watch for impossible
values (negative counts, change ratios far from a plausible range, or shares
outside [0, 1]).

```{r validate-numeric-panel}
print_numeric_summary(acs_out, "acs_full")
```

## 7.5 Optionally save and validate the canonical output

Only the existing canonical columns in `acs_full` are eligible for saving. Set
`write_panel <- TRUE` in §1.3 and rerun from setup to enable a write after reviewing
diagnostics. Existing schema checks remain strict; a missing prior reference is
reported as not checked. Replacement is announced. The reload branch runs only
after this run writes the file, and verifies keys, schema, and every saved value.

```{r save-panel}
panel_written <- FALSE
if (isTRUE(write_panel)) {
  report_n(acs_full, "Canonical ACS tract panel to save")
  audit_panel_keys(acs_full, input_keys_16, input_keys_24_bg_agg)
  report_tract_counties(acs_full, panel_counties, "Final panel destination counties")
  if (!is.null(prior_panel)) {
    assert_same_schema(acs_full, prior_panel, "Panel schema versus prior output")
  } else {
    cat("Prior panel schema comparison not checked: no existing acs_full.feather at setup.\n")
  }
  cat("Writing/replacing", file.path(data_dir, "acs_full.feather"), "\n")
  arrow::write_feather(acs_full, file.path(data_dir, "acs_full.feather"))
  panel_written <- TRUE
} else {
  cat("Canonical write disabled: validated in-memory panel; no output replaced.\n")
}
```

```{r reload-panel}
if (isTRUE(panel_written)) {
  acs_saved <- arrow::read_feather(file.path(data_dir, "acs_full.feather"))
  saved_panel_membership <- audit_panel_keys(acs_saved, input_keys_16, input_keys_24_bg_agg)
  report_tract_counties(acs_saved, panel_counties, "Saved panel destination counties")
  assert_same_schema(acs_saved, acs_full, "Saved panel schema")
  stopifnot("Saved panel values must agree with the validated in-memory panel" =
              isTRUE(all.equal(acs_saved, acs_full)))
} else {
  cat("Reload skipped: this run did not write a canonical panel.\n")
}
```
